The quoted sentence only describes the development of a vector expressing the CLN6 gene. It does not establish that CLN6 mutations cause CLN6-Batten disease. While the abstract mentions that the treatment prevents pathological hallmarks in Cln6 mutant mice, the quoted sentence alone provides no evidence of a causal relationship between CLN6 and the disease. The abstract context indicates that CLN6 deficiency causes the disease, but the specific quoted evidence does not support the 'causes' relationship.

The quoted sentence states that intrathecal delivery in non-human primates was 'safe, well tolerated, and led to efficient targeting throughout the brain and spinal cord.' These are safety and biodistribution properties, not evidence of therapeutic effect or disease treatment. The quote does not demonstrate that scAAV9.CB.hCLN6 treats CLN6-Batten disease.

The quoted sentence directly states that in Cln6 mutant mice, scAAV9.CB.CLN6 'prevented or drastically reduced all of the pathological hallmarks of Batten disease.' This demonstrates a clear therapeutic effect of the treatment on the disease phenotype. The subsequent sentence further supports this by describing improvements in motor performance, learning and memory, and survival.
